@@ mariners
The Mariners are descendants of High Man rebels who fled th southern empires. Most settled in the far south and began a lon struggle for control with the native elements. Since that tim modest inbreeding with the locals has created a somewhat distinc group, although their High Man roots remain strong. The heritage as sailors and merchantmen from the southern empire still influences their culture and lifestyle. They long to reclaim th southern empires.

@@ hysical_haracter
Build: Strong of build. Males average 215 pounds; women, 14 pounds. Coloring: Mariners are generally fair skinned and have grey o bluish eyes and black or dark brown hair. Endurance: Considerable. They do not get seasick. Height: Men average 6'3"; women, 5'9". Lifespan: 95-190 years. Resistance: Normal. Special Abilities: They get a special +20 bonus for the followin skills: Boat Piloting, Navigation, Rope Mastery, Rowing Sailing, Star Gazing, Weather Watching.

@@ ulture
Clothing & Decoration: Mariners favor purple, red, and gol clothing made from silk or fine cotton. They wear tunics an only rarely don leggings. Men wear gold collars, while wome are well-adorned with jewelry. Fears & Inabilities: Disease and illness, and their own natura mortality. Lifestyle: Mariner culture reflects the conservative ele- ments found among southern empires’ aristocracy, only it is carried to an extreme. Marriage Pattern: Monogamous. Line is traced through male. Religion: Mariner religion is preoccupied with Death and Darkness, and largely revolves around ancestor and hero worship. The great Ancient Kings are revered as god- like. Ceremonies dwell on the perpetuation of the life of the individual and, more importantly, the lineage. The dead are buried with elaborate fanfare and are laid to rest in a preserved state, one of pronounced splendor.

@@ ther_actors
Demeanor: Aggressive, haughty, determined, embit- tered—the Mariners have the attitude of royalty in unjust exile. Language: Starting Languages: High-speech (S8/W6), Al-Common-speech (S8/W6), Sea-speech (S8/W6). lowed Adolescence Development: High-speech (S10/ W10), Common-speech (S10/W10), Sea-speech (S10/ W10), South-speech (S8/W8), Wood-speech (S6/W6), Plains-speech (S6/W6). Prejudices: Their greatest enemies are the High Men, because they are held to blame for the wars of the southern empires. Professions: No special notes. Special Skills: Everyman: Rope Mastery, Rowing, Sail- ing, Star Gazing; Restricted: none.
